scenes.line1: What makes a good alert rule?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how to write alert rules that actually help, not just spam your team?

scenes.label: PromQL
scenes.sub: Alert rules use a PromQL expression to define what to watch.
scenes.say: Alert rules start with a PromQL expression. That’s how you tell the system exactly what to monitor.

rows.b: How long it must be true

scenes.say: Every alert rule has three parts: the metric to watch, how long it must stay triggered, and how serious it is.

scenes.title: Disk almost full
scenes.say: Here’s an alert for when disk space drops below ten percent for ten minutes. It’s marked as a warning.

scenes.label: for
scenes.sub: Use durations to block noisy, one-off spikes.
scenes.say: Adding a duration stops one-off spikes from waking up the whole team. It keeps alerts actionable.

scenes.question: What’s the most important part?
scenes.wrong: Severity, so you know who to page.
scenes.right: All parts matter: expression, duration, and severity. Missing any makes alerts useless or noisy.
scenes.say: Interviewers love this question. Don’t just pick severity—every part matters. Without all three, alerts get ignored or become noise.
